key_insight: Laser post-treatment reduced wear rates by approximately 24% for detonation-sprayed and 39% for gas-flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C coatings, while producing deposition-dependent mechanical changes.
engineering_relevance: Laser post-treatment offers a route to improve sliding-wear resistance on coated AISI 321 stainless steel, but deposition method matters when stiffness and hardness are design priorities.
method: Deposit coatings by detonation spraying and gas-flame spraying, then apply laser post-treatment.
Characterize microstructure and phases using SEM, EDS, and XRD.
Compare mechanical and dry-sliding performance using instrumented indentation and ball-on-disk testing.
evidence_signal: Detonation-sprayed coating hardness increased from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV; wear rates fell from 1.939 to 1.465 and from 2.419 to 1.476 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m) for detonation- and gas-flame-sprayed coatings, respectively.
watch_item: Laser treatment lowered the gas-flame-sprayed coating’s elastic modulus from 228.0 to 187.0 GPa, so improved wear resistance does not imply improved stiffness.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Post-Treatment on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation- and Flame-Sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C Coatings
